result.title: ExeWorldBench: Benchmarking Code-Based Executable 3D World Modeling
result.summary: Coding agents are increasingly evolving beyond reproducing what a world looks like toward constructing executable worlds that capture how a world works. This shift calls for executable world modeling, which integrates two core capabilities: world understanding, reasoning about the underlying structural, mechanical, and causal principles of a world, and executable realization, translating that understanding into a code-based system whose behavior emerges from physical interactions. However, existing benchmarks provide only fragmented evaluations centered on physical reasoning, visual fidelity, or behavioral correctness, leaving the integration of these capabilities insufficiently assessed. To bridge this gap, we introduce ExeWorldBench, to our knowledge the first benchmark to comprehensively evaluate world understanding and executable realization through code-based 3D world construction. ExeWorldBench comprises three progressively challenging tasks: Mechanism Executability, which evaluates the realization of individual mechanisms from visual observations; Compositional Executability, which extends to multi-stage systems with spatial, mechanical, and causal dependencies; and Intent-Driven Executable World Synthesis, which requires constructing executable worlds from high-level goals and physical requirements. Extensive experiments on frontier models reveal substantial limitations in executable world modeling, offering insights into the development of more physically grounded and causally coherent world construction systems.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 ExeWorldBench，一个通过代码构建可执行 3D 世界来评测「世界理解」（结构、机械与因果原理）与「可执行实现」的基准，含机制可执行、组合可执行与意图驱动合成三项递进任务，并报告前沿模型存在明显不足。
AI.relevance_reason: 该基准把「从视觉观察推导因果/机械结构并转写为可执行代码」作为评测信号，可能为核查 VLM 内部是否真正保留任务必要的视觉与因果信息提供外部化验证思路，但无 latent 状态或推理期机制，实际启发需进一步核查。
